truth (issue #1118): in a module that saves, a -ux handler (a method that writes with the request Context, in a
file where another method reaches a save) with no path to a station save is one WARN write-path-no-save on its
first write line, even though the module saves elsewhere: doSetpoint calls requestSave() and passes, doMode
writes and never saves. A write helper in another file that no handler of its file reaches a save from is out
of scope (the module-wide rule covers it).
-- args --
@DIR@/Mod
-- want --
exit 0
WARN  write-path-no-save  @DIR@/Mod/Mod-ux/src/com/x/ux/BDashServlet.java:11  handler writes station state with the request Context but no path from it requests a station save (requestSave() directly or through a same-module helper): that write is lost on the next restart; call requestSave() after the write succeeds, or declare persistence: <where> in MODULE-MAP.md (types/dashboard.md § Write path)
-- stderr --
-- Mod/Mod-ux/src/com/x/ux/BDashServlet.java --
package com.x.ux;
public final class BDashServlet extends BWebServlet {
  void requestSave() {
    saveTicket = Clock.schedule(station, delay, BStation.save, null);
  }
  void doSetpoint(BComponent point, BValue v, Context cx) {
    point.set("out", v, cx);
    requestSave();
  }
  void doMode(BComponent point, BValue v, Context cx) {
    point.set("mode", v, cx);
  }
}
